description: Vanilla+ Fabric RPG exploration modpack with immersive combat and optimized performance.
body:
# Ragnarok's VanFan Modpack

Ragnarok's VanFan Modpack is a lightweight Vanilla+ Fabric RPG exploration modpack for Minecraft 1.20.1 focused on immersive progression, medieval fantasy combat, exploration, atmosphere, and optimized performance.

The modpack expands Minecraft while preserving the core Vanilla experience. Explore overhauled terrain, enhanced villages, dangerous dungeons, improved Nether and End dimensions, and handcrafted structures generated by Terralith, Incendium, Nullscape, CTOV, and Dungeon Now Loading.

Progression is built around RPG-style gameplay using LevelZ, Better Combat, Epic Knights, Simply Swords, Artifacts, and AdventureZ. Players must level skills, unlock stronger equipment, discover loot, and survive increasingly dangerous adventures.

The world is designed to feel alive and immersive through Naturalist, AmbientSounds, Presence Footsteps, dynamic lighting, improved farming systems, ships, backpacks, and village improvements. Exploration and long-term survival are supported by Waystones, Xaero’s Maps, Nature’s Compass, graves, and multiple quality-of-life features.

The modpack also includes a fully optimized Fabric performance stack using Sodium, Lithium, FerriteCore, ModernFix, EntityCulling, and additional optimization mods to provide smooth gameplay on low-to-mid-end systems.

Main Features:

* Vanilla+ RPG progression
* Medieval fantasy combat
* Overhauled world generation
* Enhanced exploration and dungeons
* Improved villages and structures
* Farming, cooking, and immersive survival systems
* Dynamic lighting and atmospheric audio
* Lightweight and performance-focused
* Stable Fabric 1.20.1 experience
* Singleplayer and multiplayer friendly

Recommended:

* Minecraft 1.20.1
* Fabric Loader
* 4–6 GB RAM allocation

This modpack is intended for players who want a cohesive Vanilla+ adventure experience with exploration, progression, immersion, and stable long-term gameplay.
